what_worked: Slide 6 volume-vs-median contrast is genuinely useful; the AI Valuation Trap framing shows analytical ambition.
fix_next: Verify every median and total against the actual data; the slide-9 dashboard has obvious placeholder values that destroy credibility.
verdict: Ambitious structure undermined by numerous factual errors and uncorrected placeholder data.
factual_error_detail: Slide 4: anonymous count 130 vs reference 129, named 870 vs 871. Slide 5: Stripe (636 listings, $13.5M) entirely omitted from provider analysis; Superwall/Paddle/Whop/Creem shown as if they are the full provider landscape. Slide 6 right panel: Marketing median $1,586 vs reference $2,369.50; Education median $2,142 vs reference $2,435; Analytics median $1,294 vs reference $419; AI median $446 vs reference $503. Slide 7: E-comm median $155 vs reference $387. Slide 9 dashboard: median MRR chart shows $150 placeholder for AI/SaaS/Education/Marketing/E-comm—clearly fabricated. Slide 6 left panel: SaaS shown as #2 total revenue but Marketing ($1.32M) actually exceeds SaaS ($703K). Slide 8: calls r=0.802 subscription correlation a 'highly reliable leading indicator'—causal overreach from cross-sectional observational data.

evidence.insight: Volume-vs-median contrast on slide 6 is the strongest original contribution; E-comm skew observation on slide 7/10 adds value. But no discussion of top-10 concentration (49.6%), founded-year non-correlation, TLD analysis, or missingness impact limits depth.
evidence.narrative: Logical topic-by-topic sequence (data quality → geography → identity → providers → categories → predictors → conclusions) but no single driving question is posed or answered; reads as a report rather than a story with a thesis.
evidence.framing: Title slide says 'Strategic Financial Readout' without specifying audience or question. Slide 2 mentions domain-rating missingness but ignores category missingness (274 rows) despite heavy category analysis on slides 6-7. No limitations or caveats slide.
evidence.accuracy: At least 9 material errors spanning omitted providers, wrong medians, wrong category rankings, placeholder dashboard values, and slightly wrong anonymous/named counts. The Stripe omission alone misrepresents the payment infrastructure landscape entirely.
evidence.visual: Clean serif typography, muted blue-grey palette, appropriate chart types (bar, pie, scatter). Slide 9 dashboard is ambitious but the median MRR sub-chart has clearly broken placeholder data ($150 repeated five times). Professional layout overall but template-driven.
evidence.ai_slop: Slide 9 median MRR chart shows identical $150 for five categories—strong indicator of AI-generated placeholder never corrected. Consulting buzzwords throughout ('gold standard', 'Strategic Financial Readout', 'predictive reliability') add filler without substance.
